production.note: 18 mission-only stills for the rebuilt Unit 6 mission: a kickoff, nine listening scenes and the question and response views of four voice gates. The stub mission's plaza, school and corner scenes cannot be kept, because the approved photo-edit record for each one pins its stub card exactly as inspected, so the rebuilt beats bind their own stills and the stub scenes are retired with evidence. The kickoff fixes the family cast, and every later scene with people is generated from it. Buildings are identified by symbols and goods, never by words. No automatic retries.

shared_prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create a brand-new high-detail real photograph for a beginner English learning game, full-bleed 3:2 landscape. Natural material textures, believable optics, physically coherent light, realistic skin, anatomy and hands. This is one continuous real scene, not a collage, infographic, illustration, split-screen, panels, toy model or app screenshot. When several targets are requested they must be visually distinct at phone size, well separated left to right, with clear empty space above each target for UI markers added later, and they must never touch or overlap each other. Do not draw dots, arrows, labels, UI, speech bubbles, borders, captions or watermarks. Preserve full people including feet when visible; no cropped heads, hands or action. No padded or blurred side strips. No venue names, logos or answer words; only explicitly requested numerals may appear.

assets.prompt: Use case: text-exact. Four round analog station clocks hanging in one row on a plain station wall above an empty platform, photographed straight on in daylight, evenly spaced with clear wall between them and no people. Each clock has a plain white face, printed numerals 1 to 12, one short thick black hour hand, one long thin black minute hand and no second hand. On every clock the long minute hand lies exactly along the line from the centre to the numeral 12, pointing straight up. Each short hour hand lies exactly along the line from the centre of its dial to its own numeral, with the tip ending just short of that printed numeral: from left to right the hour hands point exactly at 7, then 8, then 9, then 10, and never between two numerals. Every face is sharp and each clock is at least 15% of the frame width. No departure board, no words, no brand names, no other numerals anywhere.
